advisory.finding: `det_citation._edge_verified` compares ticket ids with raw string equality, but stored `deps[].target_id` values are canonicalized full ids while the cited `[rebar:<id>]` token may be an alias or short-id (documented as allowed). A plan that legitimately declares `depends_on -> C` but cites `[rebar:<alias>]` will not verify under encoding (a) and gets a spurious 'unbacked citation' advisory.
scenarios: Author writes `depends_on -> 1a2b` (short-id) which reduces to canonical `1a2b-3c4d-...`, and cites `[rebar:1a2b]` — edge is real but det_citation emits a false 'no VERIFIED upstream prerequisite' advisory.
Author cites by alias (e.g. `[rebar:proscience-sudorific-rhino]`) with a declared depends_on edge stored canonically — encoding (a) misses it.
advisory.suggested_fix: Resolve `cited_id`, each `own_deps[].target_id`, and `plan_ticket_id` to canonical ids (e.g. inject a `resolve_id` callable backed by `resolve_ticket_id`, mirroring the `resolve_deps` injection) and compare canonical-to-canonical in both encodings.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a parse_citations test with two [rebar:] tokens on the same line asserting each subject excludes the other citation's token.
evidence: det_citation.py:60: `start = line_start if line_start != prev_line_start else max(line_start, prev_end)`

test_parse text has `[rebar:1234-abcd]` on one line and `[rebar:proscience-sudorific-rhino]` on the next line (test_det_citation.py:32-33), so prev_line_start != line_start always holds and the else-branch never executes
ABSENCE: no test feeds two [rebar:] tokens on the same source line to parse_citations
advisory.finding: parse_citations has a dedicated branch for two-or-more citations sharing a single line (`start = line_start if line_start != prev_line_start else max(line_start, prev_end)`), but no test exercises multiple [rebar:] tokens on the same line; test_parse places its two tokens on separate lines. A regression in the shared-line subject-slicing (e.g. re-slicing the second subject from the line start, capturing the first citation's token) would not be caught.
scenarios: A plan line citing two prerequisites, e.g. `use foo [rebar:aaaa] and bar [rebar:bbbb]`, where the second subject must exclude the first token
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a case: `parse_citations("use `foo` [rebar:aaaa-bbbb] and `bar` [rebar:cccc-dddd]")` and assert both subjects are correctly delimited and neither contains `[rebar:`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a p6_ac_quality test where ctx.state['deps'] contains a depends_on edge matching the cited id, asserting no citation issue and coverage['citation_gaps'] == 0.
evidence: test_det_floor_wires_citation uses `state={"deps": []}  # deps LACK the edge` (test_det_citation.py:105)
ABSENCE: no p6_ac_quality/run_det_floor test supplies a matching `depends_on` edge in ctx.state['deps'] and asserts citation_gaps == 0
advisory.finding: The det_floor integration test only covers the edge-UNBACKED path (state={'deps': []}); no test drives p6_ac_quality with a citation whose prerequisite edge IS verified to assert no citation issue is emitted and citation_gaps == 0. This leaves the det_floor wiring (mapping ctx.state['deps']->own_deps and ctx.ticket_id->plan_ticket_id in the unbacked_citations call) unverified for the positive case.
scenarios: A regression swapping the own_deps/ticket_id argument order, or reading the wrong key from ctx.state, would make even genuinely edge-backed citations always coach
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test mirroring test_det_floor_wires_citation but with `state={"deps": [{"relation": "depends_on", "target_id": "1111-2222"}]}` and assert `r.coverage.get('citation_gaps') == 0` and no evidence line contains `[rebar:`.
